name: Ahimaaz
source_summary: Son of Zadok the priest, known as "the runner" for his role relaying critical intelligence to David during Absalom's rebellion, including narrowly escaping capture by hiding in a well, and later outrunning another messenger to bring David news of the battle's outcome, though he could not bring himself to tell the king plainly that his son Absalom was dead.
family_friendly_summary: Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok the priest and was known for being a fast, reliable runner. During a difficult time when David's own son Absalom rebelled against him, Ahimaaz helped carry secret messages to David so he would know what Absalom's advisors were planning. Once, Ahimaaz and a friend had to hide inside a well to avoid being caught, and a brave woman covered the well's opening to help protect them. Later, after the battle where Absalom died, Ahimaaz begged to be the one to run and tell David the outcome. He ran so fast that he arrived before the other messenger, but when he reached David, he couldn't bring himself to say plainly that Absalom had died, since he knew how much it would hurt the king.
adult_story: Ahimaaz, son of Zadok the priest, served as a trusted courier for David during Absalom's rebellion. When David fled Jerusalem, he arranged for Zadok and Abiathar to stay behind with their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan as an intelligence relay, using the priests' access to the city (2 Samuel 15:27-36). The plan nearly failed: waiting outside the city at En-rogel, Ahimaaz and Jonathan were spotted and had to hide in a well at Bahurim, its opening covered with grain by a quick-thinking woman, before delivering word that let David escape across the Jordan ahead of Absalom's pursuit (17:17-22). After the decisive battle in the forest of Ephraim, Ahimaaz begged Joab to let him run and report the victory to David, even though Joab initially refused him, choosing a Cushite messenger instead since "the king's son is dead" and there would be no reward in that news (18:19-23). Ahimaaz ran anyway, by a faster route, and reached David first -- but when the king anxiously asked whether Absalom was safe, Ahimaaz could not bring himself to answer plainly, saying only that he saw "a great tumult" (18:28-29). The Cushite arrived moments later with the truth. Ahimaaz's swift loyalty throughout the rebellion, paired with his inability to speak the hardest news to a grieving father, paints one of Scripture's more human character sketches among David's supporting cast.
devotionals: Ahimaaz’s story teaches us about messenger; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Ahimaaz’s experience of Absalom's rebellion, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
